faq: Do I need an eBay Store subscription?
It is optional. A store gives lower fees in some categories and extra tools, but costs a monthly fee. We compare your sales volume against the tiers so you can decide if it pays off.
Can you set up the store if I have no listings yet?
Yes. We build the design and category tree first, then your listings drop in as you add them. Add the listing creation service if you also want us to write the first items.
Can I use my brand's logo?
Yes, if you own it or have the right to use it. Send us the files, or we make a simple text logo. We cannot use another brand's name or logo in your store design, as eBay forbids that.
Will the store look good on mobile?
Yes. eBay shows stores in its own mobile layout, so we design the banner to crop well and keep text short and centered. We check it on a phone before we hand it over.
desc:
An eBay Store setup, with design and categories, gives buyers one tidy place to browse everything you sell. Ecom Swift LLC sets up your store in your own eBay account with a banner, logo, store categories, featured items, an About section and matching policies.

## What is an eBay Store?

An eBay Store is a branded storefront inside eBay, available through a subscription you choose directly with eBay. It gathers your listings under your own name, with a banner, a logo, your own categories and an About section. Buyers who like one item can browse the rest without returning to search results.

We do not buy the subscription for you. We guide you on which tier fits your volume and then build the store inside it.

## Why a store layout helps buyers find more of your items

Without a store, each listing stands alone. A buyer who finds one item has no easy path to the others. With a store, they see your categories at the top, your featured items and your branding, and the whole range feels like one business.

Store categories are the main tool. They let a buyer move from your front page to the right group of items in a click or two. If categories are confusing or too few, shoppers leave. If they are clear, shoppers stay and look at more of what you sell.

## How the store affects trust and repeat visits

A consistent banner, logo and About section tell a visitor that a real business is behind the listings. Policies that match across the store reduce surprises, and a clear return and shipping policy answers questions before they are asked.

A store also helps repeat buyers. They can bookmark it, find new items quickly and see what you feature. We cannot promise more sales, because that depends on your items, prices and competition, but a clear store removes friction between a buyer's interest and the next listing they open.

## What a good eBay Store includes

- A store name and web address option that is short and easy to remember.
- A logo that stays clear at small sizes.
- A banner designed to eBay's size rules.
- Store categories organized around how buyers think, not how you stock.
- Listings sorted into those categories.
- Featured items on the front page.
- An About section with a short, honest introduction.
- Payment, shipping and return policies applied consistently.
- Promotion boxes and a header where your package includes them.

## What we do

We begin with a short brief about your range and brand. We then suggest a store name and address options, prepare the logo and banner, and plan a category structure on paper before building it in your account. You see the plan first and can change it.

In the Basic package we set up the brand, a small set of categories and policies. In the Standard package we add more categories, sort listings, set featured items and an About section and advise on subscription tier. In the Premium package we build a fuller structure with promotion boxes, a store header and a style guide for future listings.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Name categories with the words buyers would use.
- Keep the number of top-level categories small.
- Feature a few items that show the range well.
- Keep the banner simple and readable on a phone.
- Update featured items when stock changes.

**Avoid:**
- Creating a category for a single item.
- Using clever category names that buyers will not search for.
- Crowding the banner with text and offers.
- Using a logo you do not have the right to use.
- Choosing a subscription tier before you know your volume.

## Who this is for

This service suits a seller whose range has outgrown a handful of listings. It suits a small brand that wants eBay to look as organized as its own website, and a new seller preparing a store before the first big batch of listings.

## What we need from you

Tell us what you sell, share your logo and brand colors if you have them and send a list or export of your listings. Tell us which tier you plan to subscribe to, or ask us for advice. We never ask for your password. We work in your eBay account as a limited user, and the store always remains yours.
